tagline.text: A quiet limestone island in the northern Cebu sea with the Laaw Lagoon and cliff-lined shores

location.label: Location
location.text: Santa Fe, Cebu (east of Bantayan Island), across from Mahayahay Port in Daanbantayan

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000~2,500 (day trip from Cebu City, per person)

children.text: Kinatarcan is a limestone island of about 7 km in length off the northwest of mainland Cebu. It has the emerald Laaw Lagoon, coastal cliffs, a stair-access beach and a sunset beach, but no resorts and no ATMs, so it is a remote trip.
Kinatarcan Island (also spelled Kinatarkan, Guintacan or Guintarcan) is a limestone island in the Visayan Sea, about
25 km
west of mainland Cebu and about
12 km

northeast of Bantayan Island. It belongs to the municipality of Santa Fe at the southeastern end of Bantayan Island, and has three barangays: Langub, Hagdan and Kinatarcan (the central village on the Bitoon Beach side). According to Wikipedia, the island covers about 13 km², stretching in an elongated oval about
6.8 km
north to south and
2.5 km
east to west.

The face of the island is the Laaw Lagoon on the east coast. In its shallow emerald water, surrounded by limestone cliffs and trees, residents grow edible seaweed (lato). Recent travel accounts say swimming inside the lagoon is no longer allowed, so it is safer to treat it as a place for a short walk and scenery rather than a swim. The coast alternates between tall cliffs and occasional flat beaches, with coral reefs and seagrass beds offshore.

This is not a resort destination lined with hotels like Malapascua or Bantayan. There are no large resorts, only small eateries, the mobile signal is weak and there are no ATMs. It will not suit anyone who expects amenities, but for travelers who want an uncrowded sea, cliffs and a fishing-village atmosphere, it is one of the quietest choices in northern Cebu.

The boat from Mahayahay Port in Daanbantayan on mainland Cebu takes about an hour, and the island can also be reached from Santa Fe on Bantayan Island. The fares and times in this guide are compiled from several travel accounts dated between 2018 and 2026, so some values are out of date. Please check again locally before you go.

This shallow emerald lagoon ringed by limestone cliffs is the most visited spot on the island. The water color is clearest around noon or at high tide. Because it is a seaweed farm, swimming is reportedly prohibited, so enjoy it with photos and a walk.

A steep cliff viewpoint a short walk through thickets from Laaw Lagoon. Visitors say you can carefully climb down over fallen boulders and swim beneath carved-looking rock walls. The rocks are sharp, so wear shoes.

Pasil Beach in Barangay Langub is where most travelers first step off the boat. D'Clam Cave on the beach has an underground saltwater pool, giant clam fossils and clay used for mud masks, and the entrance fee is listed at about
About 100 steps along the cliff lead down to a long white-sand beach. It lies south of Laaw Lagoon and is quiet with few visitors. The climb back up can be tiring, so bring water.

This beach faces west, so it is good for watching the sunset and also suits swimming and relaxing. Forest Beach Guesthouse, which offers lodging, is on this side. It reportedly also has a jumping board, hammocks and grilling spots.
Langub is a fishing settlement, and dried fish (bulad) is the island's signature souvenir. It is polite to ask permission before taking photos.

blocks.title: Langub Cliffs and Tamboan ni Leon

children.text: Langub Cliffs are about 4–6 m high, with deep water and corals below. The Coral Cliff (Tamboan ni Leon) is about 15–18 m high and reportedly has strong wind and waves. The path is steep and rough, so going with a guide is safer.

Collared kingfishers have been observed at Laaw Lagoon, and there are records of the critically endangered Christmas Island frigatebird. The Guintarcan lighthouse stands on the southeast side of the island. Early morning is best for birdwatching.

items.title: Day route
items.subtitle: Leave Cebu City on a morning bus

children.text: Take a bus to Daanbantayan from the North Bus Terminal in Cebu City. The air-conditioned bus takes about
4 hours
, and since boats to the island run only in the morning, you are advised to leave no later than
. Get off in front of the Daanbantayan market.
From the market, take a tricycle or motorcycle to Mahayahay Port. The fare is about
. Look for a boat to Pasil Beach or Hagdan Beach among the passenger boats lined up at the port.
The boat ride of about
1 hour
brings you to Pasil Beach. Pay the environmental and entrance fees and visit D'Clam Cave first.
Ride a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) to Laaw Lagoon. The water color is best around noon. Do not swim; spend your time walking and taking photos.
Walk to the Biaring Cliff viewpoint, and if the way is safe, look at the rocky shore below. For lunch, ask a local shop to cook the food you brought, or use a small eatery.
Go down the Hagdan Beach steps and rest, then move to Bitoon Beach and stay until sunset. Be sure to confirm the return boat time.
One record from 2018 says the regular return boat leaves at
in the morning only, so a day trip is tight unless you charter a boat. Either stay overnight or arrange a chartered boat in advance.

items.title: Two days, one night
items.subtitle: Relaxed, with a stay at Bitoon Beach

children.text: Leave Cebu City early and reach the island via Daanbantayan, Mahayahay Port and the boat. Drop your bags at your lodging on Bitoon Beach.
Visit Langub fishing village, Pasil Beach and D'Clam Cave, then ride a habal-habal around Laaw Lagoon and Biaring Cliff.
Watch the sunset at Bitoon Beach and have dinner at your lodging.
See the Hagdan Beach steps and viewpoint, then head to the port in time for the morning boat. If you miss it, you will have to find a chartered boat.
A 2018 record says you can camp with your own tent for a fee of about
, but it has not been confirmed whether that is still the case.
There are several domestic flights a day from Manila (NAIA) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), taking about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Check the airlines' current schedules.
From the airport, take a taxi or ride-hailing car to the North Bus Terminal in Cebu City. Depending on traffic, it takes around
1 hour
Flying is the most practical way to get from Manila to Cebu.
Take a bus bound for Daanbantayan from the North Bus Terminal (near SM City Cebu). The air-conditioned bus takes about
4 hours
The fare was recorded as
in 2018 but may have risen since. Check before boarding.
Tell the driver to drop you at the Daanbantayan market.

items.title: Boat from Daanbantayan to the island

At the port, board a shared pump boat to Pasil Beach or Hagdan Beach. It takes about
1 hour
and is recorded at about
one way.
If you are in a group, you can also rent a whole boat, reported at about
round trip for up to 20 people.
Shared boats cluster in the morning, so arrive at the port early.
Regular boats from Santa Fe Port to Bitoon Beach are said to run daily. Chartered boats are also possible on request.
Schedules and fares can change, so check at Santa Fe Port.
On the island, habal-habal (motorcycle taxis) are the main transport. A habal-habal island tour was recorded at about
Groups can rent a pump boat or a multicab.
Considering boats and weather, the dry season from November to May is the most stable. At this time the sea is calm and the Laaw Lagoon's water color is good.
From June to October there is more rain and wind, and the sea gets rough, so small pump boats may be canceled or delayed. If you go in this period, check the weather at the port the day before.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Boats are stable and sunsets are beautiful. The most recommended period.
The water color is good, but the midday sun is strong, so a hat and sunscreen are essential.
Boats may be canceled. Check the weather and leave room in your schedule.

There are no large resorts on the island. Forest Beach Guesthouse on Bitoon Beach is described as a lodging overlooking the sea that offers swimming and guided habal-habal tours, and a room was recorded at about
in 2021. We recommend contacting them in advance to book before peak season.

Food is limited to snacks, canned goods and drinks sold in small shops. Most travelers buy raw ingredients or packed meals at the Daanbantayan market and ask residents to cook them. In Langub you can buy dried fish (bulad) as a souvenir. Fresh water is scarce, so bring plenty of drinking water.
Withdraw enough cash before departure at Landbank or Prince Hypermart (China Bank ATM) in Daanbantayan. There are no ATMs on the island and the mobile signal is weak.
Boats to the island cluster in the morning, so it is best to leave Cebu City at dawn.
Bring plenty of drinking water, snacks, sunscreen and a hat. Fresh water is scarce on the island.
Cliffs and rocks are sharp, so wear water shoes or sturdy shoes.
Laaw Lagoon is a seaweed farm, and swimming is reportedly prohibited. Follow local guidance before entering.
If the lagoon gate is locked, ask the barangay hall or the caretaker for the key and check whether there is a fee.
Take all your trash back with you. Respect the islanders' way of life and beliefs.
The return boat leaves early, so confirm the boat time the day before your last day.
The Biaring Cliff and Tamboan ni Leon areas have sharp rocks and strong waves, and guides reportedly will not take anyone who has been drinking. Do not climb down alone.
Medical facilities on the island could not be confirmed. Bring basic medicines and emergency contacts.
On small pump boats, ask for a life jacket and check that the boat is not overloaded.
If boats are canceled in bad weather, you may have to stay another night on the island, so leave room in your schedule.
Fares and rules (lagoon access, the swimming ban, boat times) come from sources of different years. Check the latest announcements.
Contact details for private guides and lodging come from personal blogs and may change. Be sure to confirm them in advance.
A large island about
1 hour
away by boat with many beach resorts and lodgings, which pairs well with Kinatarcan.
A diving island at the northern tip of Cebu, reached by boat from another port in Daanbantayan. Consider it if you extend your trip.
The mainland town where boats to the island depart. It is a good place to buy ingredients at the market and withdraw cash.
